approach: A culture and vocabulary lesson: the common nicknames built on Spanish first names (Pepe, Paco, Lupita, Chuy and others), the -ito / -ita diminutive, and when using them is warm versus too familiar.
coverage: Many Spanish first names have a traditional nickname
Pepe = José; Paco and Pancho = Francisco; Lupe and Lupita = Guadalupe; Chuy = Jesús (Mexico)
More: Nacho = Ignacio; Lola = Dolores; Memo = Guillermo; Lalo = Eduardo; Toño = Antonio; Beto = Alberto or Roberto
The -ito / -ita ending makes an affectionate form: Juanito, Anita, Carlitos
Some nicknames are regional; Chuy, Memo and Lalo are typically Mexican
Use a nickname when the person uses it or invites you to; use the full name in formal settings

blocks.purpose: Explains Spanish nicknames and why they can look unrelated to the name.

paragraphs: Spanish speakers often use a traditional nickname (un apodo, or in grammar a hipocorístico) for a first name. Some are easy to see, like Lupita for Guadalupe. Others look unrelated: Pepe is José and Paco is Francisco.
You will hear them among family, friends and coworkers. When someone introduces themself with a nickname, use it; in formal settings and on documents, use the full name.

data.title: Call me Pepe
data.cueNote: Todos me dicen Pepe: everyone calls me Pepe. Para los amigos: to his friends.

cues.text: Me llamo José, pero todos me dicen Pepe.
Soy Guadalupe. Mis amigos me dicen Lupita.
Él es Francisco, Paco para los amigos.
Mi hermano Jesús es Chuy en la familia.

data.anchor: Adding -ito or -ita to a name makes an affectionate form, often for children or close family.
prerequisites: Juan → Juanito; Ana → Anita; Carlos → Carlitos.
The same ending makes things small or dear: un momento → un momentito (wait a moment: un momentito).

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Knowing the nickname makes it tempting to use it to sound warm.
data.correctReasoning: In a first, formal meeting use the title and surname. Switch to Pepe only if he uses it or invites you to.
data.recoveryTip: Wait to be invited: "Dígame Pepe" or, between friends, "Dime Pepe" (Call me Pepe).

data.takeaway: Pepe is José, Paco is Francisco, Lupita is Guadalupe and Chuy is Jesús: use a nickname when the person does, and the full name when it is formal.
